newsitem.title: KENYA: Britain urges Kenya to cut corruption.
newsitem.headline: Britain urges Kenya to cut corruption.

text.p: British business leaders urged Kenya on Tuesday to improve infrastructure and cut corruption in order to encourage investment in this East African country.

"Infrastructure is known to be deficient in Kenya and corruption is also of concern," Martin Laing, chairman of the British Overseas Trade Board (BOTK), said at the opening of "Britain-in-Kenya" trade exhibition in the capital Nairobi.
Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi said it was known to Kenyans that infrastructure rehabilitation posed "a great challenge" and was one of Kenya's major priorities.

Britain is Kenya's top trading partner, with over one billion pounds ($1.62 billion) worth of investments and combined trade of over 430 million pounds in 1996, of which 191 million pounds were Kenyan exports to Britain.
